feedback.issueBody:
## Problem

The iOS Expo export fails because Apple authentication 2.5.1 imports prop-types without providing it, and Little Say's workspace does not declare the runtime dependency. The same failure reproduces on current master and PR35; it was introduced with the merged account integration and is separate from prompt-resource extraction.

The user explicitly approved a separate dependency-fix PR on October 8. [Retained baseline and PR35 reproduction logs](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/524cf7aa5866abf105537e882192325ca812615e/README.md#results) show module resolution failing in AppleButton.ios.js.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Declare the missing maintained runtime dependency in the appropriate mobile application manifest and update the lockfile proportionately.
- A fresh locked installation must complete the iOS JavaScript export without the missing-module error.
- Preserve web/Android exports, account provider behavior and applicable repository/release checks.
- Keep the published change focused: no unrelated dependency upgrades, lockfile churn, provider redesign or PR35 prompt edits.
- Do not claim signed iOS/TestFlight delivery or real Apple sign-in from a successful JavaScript export.

## Implementation plan

Verify current master and the exact Apple authentication import/dependency graph. Add the smallest production dependency declaration needed by the mobile app, regenerate the lockfile with the repository's expected package-manager version and inspect the complete dependency diff. Reproduce with a fresh locked install and run iOS, web and Android exports plus relevant checks. Keep failed-baseline and successful-final logs in accessible retained evidence outside product history.

No credentials, signed build, paid cloud build, provider call, release or deployment is needed or authorized.

## Implementing Codex task

Verified implementing task ID: `01a11ca6-7faa-7628-8031-ac89bc018019`. [Original assignment and account-owner history](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/c66f538eee183044c8a7a65eee7e4900759c9286/original-issue43.json) are preserved.

## Implementing PR

[PR44 — restore iOS export with the missing Apple authentication runtime dependency](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/44).
feedback.prBody:
## Summary

Little Say's iOS JavaScript export fails because Apple authentication imports `prop-types`, but the installed dependency graph does not provide it. Declare it as a mobile production dependency so clean locked installations can bundle the existing Apple authentication code.

The lockfile adds only `prop-types` 15.8.1 and its required nested `react-is` 16.13.1. Existing package versions, integrity hashes and classifications are unchanged; no provider code changes are needed.

Closes #43.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install baseline and final source independently with `npm ci`, then resolve the import from AppleButton and export iOS. | Baseline fails with missing `prop-types`. Final resolves version 15.8.1 and its required APIs, then completes the full iOS JavaScript export. Neither installation uses copied or junctioned dependencies. | [Before/After output and reproduction](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/README.md#before-and-after-observable-contract) |
| Export Android/web and run repository checks from the fresh final installation. | Both exports pass, along with 288 tests, type checks, server build and release metadata validation. | [Native exports](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/issue43-native-exports.log) · [Repository checks](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/issue43-check.log) |

This is non-UI dependency resolution; real CLI output is the observable Before/After contract. [Provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/provenance.json) binds actual master `fabb925c`, final source `a570b52c`, independent installations, commands and bundle hashes.

## Limitations

JavaScript export success does not establish a signed iOS build, TestFlight readiness, device behavior or real Apple sign-in. Those checks were not performed. No credentials, provider setup, cloud build, release or deployment is included.

Implementing task: `01a11ca6-7faa-7628-8031-ac89bc018019`. Independent review and CI results are recorded in the PR discussion.
